normalization.relation: entity(entity_id, Name, Aliases, Kind, Description, Project[], Source)
normalization.violation: Aliases is a `, `-joined list inside one rich_text cell.
normalization.rule: A relation is in 1NF when every attribute holds a single atomic value.
normalization.anomaly: No predicate can ask "which entity owns the alias SVC-4470". A `contains` filter matches substrings, so it also returns entities whose alias merely contains that text, and the caller has to re-split the cell and check exactly. Two entities can hold the same alias and nothing notices.
normalization.fix: Project the list into ENTITY_ALIAS(entity_id, alias) with a unique index on alias.
normalization.surviveNote: Deliberate, and documented. A multi_select would need a dataSources.update round trip per new alias, which for free-form aliases is a schema migration per fact.
normalization.citation: src/core/entity.ts — "Aliases stored on a single rich_text cell as `, `-joined."

normalization.relation: memory(memory_id, ..., Tags, Compare Notes, page blocks)
normalization.violation: Three more repeating groups: Tags as a multi_select, Compare Notes as append-only NDJSON in one cell, and the revision chain as page blocks.
normalization.anomaly: Compare Notes is an audit table inside a 2 000-character cell; Lore's own comment records that "append-past-cap throws". The revision chain is prose, so "what did this runbook say in March" is not a query anyone can write.
normalization.fix: MEMORY_TAG, MEMORY_COMPARISON and MEMORY_REVISION, one relation each.
normalization.surviveNote: Structural. A page body is not a column, and Notion offers no child table.

normalization.relation: fact(fact_id, Subject, Predicate, Object, SubjectKey, DedupKey, ...)
normalization.violation: SubjectKey and DedupKey are stored derivations of the other columns.
normalization.rule: A derived attribute should be a view, not a stored column, unless the store cannot index the expression.
normalization.anomaly: The store cannot. There are no expression indexes, so the expression is materialised, can drift from its source, and needs a backfill migration (`lore migrate --dedup-keys`) for every row written before it existed.
normalization.fix: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON fact (lower(subject), predicate, lower(object)). One line, no column, no migration.
normalization.surviveNote: A faithful workaround for a real limitation, and the clearest single example of the substrate showing through the schema.

normalization.violation: SubjectEntity → Subject. The determinant is not a candidate key.
normalization.rule: A relation is in BCNF when every determinant is a candidate key.
normalization.anomaly: Subject is a title string and SubjectEntity is a relation to the canonical row; the relation determines the string. `mergeEntities` repoints every fact relation from loser to winner and never rewrites the title, so after a merge the vault holds facts whose title says one name and whose relation points at another. §7.2 counts them.
normalization.fix: Drop the Subject string; derive it from the relation at read time.
normalization.surviveNote: Structural. Every Notion database needs a title property, and a title property cannot be a relation.
normalization.citation: src/core/entity-merge.ts — the merge moves fact relations and aliases; the word Subject does not appear in it.

normalization.violation: Confidence Score is a stored derivation of citation, contradiction and decay events that are not themselves stored.
normalization.rule: A stored derivation is only safe when its inputs are stored and the derivation is recomputable.
normalization.anomaly: The score is a state machine over an event stream, so two vaults that saw the same evidence in a different order hold different scores for the same fact. Nothing can recompute or audit it. Lore ships `lore migrate --audit-fact-confidence`, which reports the distribution rather than the correctness.
normalization.fix: Store the citations, contradictions and touches; make the score a view over them.
normalization.surviveNote: The score is then excluded from ranking anyway — confidenceFactor returns 1.0 for every value.

normalization.relation: The schema the SQLite and PostgreSQL arms execute.
normalization.rule: Every repeating group is a relation; every derivation is an index or a view; every determinant is a candidate key.
normalization.fix: This is what the reimplementation runs.

fds.rhs: title, kind, source, status, author, agent, session, topic_key, revision_count, body

fds.note: Lore's upsert key. Its own comment: "Notion provides no per-key uniqueness enforcement." §6.3 breaks it.

fds.rhs: subject, predicate, object, valid_from, valid_until, observed_at, invalidated_at, confidence, confidence_score

fds.note: The determinant is not a candidate key of FACT.
An expression index written as columns.
Coalescing key. Nothing makes it unique.
Lore is explicit: "aliases are deliberately not unique across entities."

invariants.statement: At most one memory per (topic_key, project set).
invariants.admitted: Two parallel saves with the same topicKey can both find no existing match and both create fresh rows.

invariants.statement: Every fact's Source references a memory that exists.
invariants.declarative: FOREIGN KEY (source_memory_id) REFERENCES memory ON DELETE RESTRICT
invariants.enforcedBy: nothing; `lore debt scan` finds the orphans afterwards

invariants.statement: A subject holds at most one object per functional predicate at any instant.
invariants.declarative: EXCLUDE USING gist (subject_entity_id WITH =, predicate WITH =, validity WITH &&)
invariants.enforcedBy: nothing; `lore conflicts scan` finds the contradictions afterwards, capped at 500 candidates per project
invariants.breaks: two agents asserting different owners without closing the first interval

invariants.enforcedBy: Notion select options, which an editor may extend by hand in the UI
invariants.breaks: a human typing a new option into the property

invariants.statement: An alias identifies exactly one entity.
invariants.enforcedBy: nothing — and Lore states the invariant does not hold
invariants.breaks: two entities independently claiming the same alias

invariants.declarative: CHECK (valid_until IS NULL OR valid_from <= valid_until)
invariants.enforcedBy: not verifiable from the source we read

invariants.declarative: GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED, or a plain expression index
invariants.enforcedBy: FactService.create at write time, plus a backfill migration for older rows
invariants.breaks: a write that bypasses the service — a hand edit in the Notion UI

rich_text.label: rich_text
rich_text.note: Truncated at 2 000 characters by the API.

number.label: number

postgres.sql: ALTER TABLE fact ADD CONSTRAINT ck_validity CHECK (valid_until IS NULL OR valid_from <= valid_until)

ALTER TABLE fact ADD CONSTRAINT ex_fact_validity
  EXCLUDE USING gist (
    subject_entity_id WITH =,
    predicate WITH =,
    int8range(COALESCE(valid_from, -999999), COALESCE(valid_until, 999999), '[)') WITH &&
  ) WHERE (predicate IN ('owned_by','is_a','created_by') AND subject_entity_id IS NOT NULL)
postgres.note: A temporal primary key. SQLite has no exclusion constraints; Notion has no constraints.

addConstraintToExistingVault.detail: Key (subject_entity_id, predicate, int8range(COALESCE(valid_from, '-999999'::integer::bigint), COALESCE(valid_until, 999999::bigint), '[)'::text))=(ent_0003an, owned_by, [177,295)) conflicts with key (subject_entity_id, predicate, int8range(COALESCE(valid_from, '-999999'::integer::bigint), COALESCE(valid_until, 999999::bigint), '[)'::text))=(ent_0003an, owned_by, [205,330)).

postgres.note: EXCLUDE USING gist over int8range. The write that would create the contradiction is the write that fails.

merge.note: In SQL a merge is three UPDATEs and a DELETE inside one transaction. In Notion it is one PATCH per affected page, non-atomic, at three requests per second.

anomaly.note: A correction updates the Fact row. Nothing updates the prose that restated it.

sql.note: SELECT entity_id FROM entity_alias WHERE alias = ?. With a unique index the planner returns one row and reads one page.

bitemporal.note: The two axes disagree often enough that choosing between them is a correctness decision, not a formality.

fulltext.note: FTS5 does not stem by default; to_tsvector('english', ...) does. The same phrase, over the same text, is a different query in each engine — and the answer the agent reasons from changes with it.

titleOnly.note: What the search endpoint actually does. It matches titles, so it finds a memory only when the answer is already in its name.

invertedIndex.note: One statement against a GIN or FTS5 index over the same text.

storage.note: Bodies dominate. A memory is mostly the sentence somebody wrote, which is why an inverted index over bodies is the index that matters and the one the substrate does not offer.

limits.note: Bodies are page blocks, not rich_text properties, so the 2 000-character property limit does not bind them. It binds every property Lore stores as text.
